clue.text: Exchange those captured in conflict to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the letters are read upwards, so from the bottom

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war

explanation.surface: A prisoner swap agreed between warring sides on the northern front.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to the north' asks you to write POWS bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Swop is a variant spelling of swap, to trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Sounds like standard shot at billiards?

indicators.note: the clue opens by telling us the next word's synonym is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a canon is a rule or standard

explanation.surface: Asks whether a regulation stroke in billiards is what is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: CANON (a standard) is said the same way as the answer, which has a double N.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a cannon is a shot where the cue ball strikes two other balls in turn.

clue.text: Eccentric buys teapot in Dedham Vale for one

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd, so the following letters are rearranged into an odd order

explanation.surface: An oddball tourist purchases a teapot while visiting a corner of rural England.
explanation.walkthrough: Dedham Vale is a protected landscape on the Essex–Suffolk border, famous from Constable's paintings; 'for one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a scenic place visitors seek out, and Dedham Vale is a well-known instance.

clue.text: Very famous section of Rubicon I crossed

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Evokes Caesar's famous crossing of the Rubicon, told in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is so widely celebrated it has become a symbol, i.e. extremely well known.

clue.text: Spot feathers in sink

parts.note: a spot of liquid is a drop
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: A mark of feathers spotted in a kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink is to fall or descend to a lower level, which is to drop down.

clue.text: A service set up miles away

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means raising the letters so they read upward

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis serve hit from a great distance, or a service arranged far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb for at a great distance, so it can stand in for being far off.

clue.text: Loss of confidence arising from earlier charge in court

indicators.note: these letters sit in the court abbreviation, split around them

parts.note: old can mean former or earlier
a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: Someone loses nerve after an old charge comes up in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting cold feet is an idiom for losing nerve before a commitment.

clue.text: Fairly easily, more or less

parts.note: pretty means fairly, as in pretty good
well can mean easily, as in you could well do it

explanation.surface: Reads as a hedged description of doing something without much trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty well is an idiom for almost or approximately, the same as roughly.

clue.text: Sea creature — sound of body following rear of dhow

indicators.note: the healthy word comes after the dhow letter
the rear of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of dhow
hale means healthy, sound in body

explanation.surface: A sea animal heard calling behind an Arab sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' suggests a homophone, but 'sound of body' simply means healthy. A dhow is an Arab sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale is a large marine mammal, an example of a sea creature.

clue.text: Cooking ingredient for cauldron a daughter omitted, sadly

indicators.note: omitted says the A and the daughter letter are left out of the pool
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the remaining letters are reshuffled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A witch's recipe lacking an ingredient, ruined because the daughter left it out.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool FOR and CAULDRON, remove A and D, and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflour is a fine starch used in kitchens to thicken sauces.

clue.text: Writer, Gunter, not half impressing international publisher

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so one letter goes inside the shortened name
only half the letters of the name are kept, the front half

parts.note: first half of Gunter

explanation.surface: An author named Gunter gets half-way to impressing a big international publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: Penguin is a well-known British paperback publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin Books is a major publishing house, so it is an example of a publisher.

clue.text: I perform wearing jaunty gemstone

indicators.note: the outer word wears the inner letters like clothing

parts.note: pert means lively or jaunty
to do is to perform, as in do a play

explanation.surface: A performer sporting a jaunty gemstone on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green semi-precious stone, a variety of olivine.

clue.text: Like a small iced cake

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small decorated cake

explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as a comparison, but it is a verb meaning to be keen on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to be attracted to as a verb, and as a noun a small decorated sponge cake.

clue.text: Outspoken in support of the short orderly

parts.note: being for something means supporting it

indicators.note: a short word has lost its last letter

parts.note: right means in proper order, as in put right

explanation.surface: A frank remark backing a short hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital attendant, but here it is the adjective meaning in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A forthright person speaks plainly and directly, without evasion.

clue.text: Grumpy note, last of many

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of many

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered message, the final one of a long series.
explanation.walkthrough: A crotchet is the British name for a quarter note.
explanation.definitionFit: Crotchety means irritable and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Clubs bar Richard, a smartypants

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a lever is a bar used to prise
Dick is a pet form of Richard

explanation.surface: Nightclubs barring a man named Richard because he is a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever dick is British slang for an irritating know-all who shows off.

clue.text: Focus on party that provides temporary refuge

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece being on another puts it after it

parts.note: a reception is a formal party
a centre is a focus or focal point

explanation.surface: Concentrating on a party which offers people somewhere to stay briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a place that provides short-term shelter, typically for refugees or the homeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception centre is a facility giving newly arrived or displaced people interim shelter.

clue.text: Excellent winner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as an informal adjective for first-rate
second meaning: one who wins a contest

explanation.walkthrough: The adjectival sense is old-fashioned British slang, as in 'that's champion'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a title-holder and a dated adjective for splendid.

clue.text: Experience confrontation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an event one goes through
second meaning: an ... can be a clash or skirmish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Experience' must be read as a noun, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an occurrence or happening, and also a hostile clash such as a border incident.

clue.text: Find out cheat exploited grief

parts.note: to hear is to learn or find out, as in hear news

indicators.note: exploited means worked or used, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Discovering that a cheat took advantage of someone's sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish or sorrow.

clue.text: European failing to pass

parts.note: a lapse is a failing or slip

explanation.surface: A European student who keeps failing an exam he needs to pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse or pass when it goes by.

clue.text: Sly type heading off for stand

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off means it is removed

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, crafty person

explanation.surface: A crafty character slipping away before taking a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds an artist's canvas.

clue.text: Absolutely right boy collecting trophy

indicators.note: the boy word collects, i.e. takes inside it, the trophy word

parts.note: a son is a boy
a pot is slang for a sports trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A son picking up a trophy he fully deserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is British slang meaning exactly correct.

clue.text: Suggested Independent politician was economical with the truth?

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent in election results
an MP is a Member of Parliament
a famous euphemism for lied

explanation.surface: An independent MP accused of being less than honest, with a question mark for the euphemism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Economical with the truth' became a famous political euphemism for lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Implied means indicated indirectly, the same as hinted at.

clue.text: English county and a Midwest US state

parts.note: IOW stands for the Isle of Wight, a county off England's south coast

explanation.surface: Pairs an English county with an American state, as if in a geography list.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island county in the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the states of the American Midwest.

clue.text: Robot in Dr No novel brought in to help

indicators.note: these letters are brought into the help word

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A robot appearing in a Bond novel to assist the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like Ian Fleming's book Dr No, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look like a human.

clue.text: Nobleman expected to receive king

indicators.note: the expected word receives the king letter inside it

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An aristocrat waiting for the monarch to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is a peer of the highest hereditary rank below a prince.

clue.text: Deceives gangsters storing whiskey in heart of speakeasy

indicators.note: the gangster word stores the other letters inside it

parts.note: hoods is slang for gangsters
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: middle letter of speakeasy

explanation.surface: Prohibition-era mobsters hiding liquor in an illegal bar while fooling people.
explanation.walkthrough: A speakeasy was an illicit bar during US Prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to trick or dupe someone.

clue.text: Staff not working properly in Perth?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in Australian slang ... means broken or unwell

explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Australian city, flagging Aussie slang; 'Staff' suggests employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a hooked shepherd's stick, and in Australia describes something faulty or someone ill.
